name: switch
purpose: Control-only pill toggle `Switch` (36×20 px). Two visual types: `default` (plain handle) and `privacy` (handle carries a `pi-lock` / `pi-lock-open` icon mirroring the toggled state). No label or description — wrap it in a horizontal `Field` or a `Field.Label` choice card for labeled layouts, or place it bare where the label already exists outside the control (an ItemGroup row names the field with `Item.Title`). Because the bare form has no wrapper to defer to, the control owns its own `disabled` state.
useWhen: An on/off setting that takes effect as soon as it flips (enable a feature, turn a rule on).
A row that already names the setting outside the control, such as an `item` row whose title is the label.
A visibility or access toggle: `kind="privacy"` shows a closed lock when off and an open lock when on.
avoidWhen: The toggle needs its own label, description, or helper text in a form → wrap it in a horizontal `field` (`Field orientation="horizontal"` + `Field.Content`).
The toggle should sit in a bordered card with a description → use a `field` choice card (`Field.Label` wrapping a horizontal `Field`).
A text value that only applies while a feature is on → compose a `Field` with an `InputGroup` (`InputGroup.Input` + an `InputGroup.Addon` holding the switch).
The choice is submitted with a form instead of applied immediately → use `checkbox`.
related: field` — a horizontal `Field` gives the switch its label and description; a `Field.Label` wrapping it is a card-style option.
input-group` — a text input with a trailing switch addon that enables it, inside a `Field`.
checkbox` — boolean selection submitted with a form.
item` — list row whose title names a bare switch.
bestPractices: The switch renders no text: give it an accessible name with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label.
Set `disabled` on the switch itself; it renders a native disabled button, so it leaves the tab order and ignores clicks and keys.
focused` moves real focus and forces the ring; use it only to mirror an external focus state, never as decoration.
Keep `kind="default"` unless the setting is about visibility or access.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Toggled-on state. Bind with `v-model="value"`. Mirrors the Figma checked/on variant.

props.name: kind
props.doc: Visual variant. `privacy` renders a lock icon inside the handle (closed when off, open when on).

props.name: focused
props.doc: Forces the focused visual state regardless of keyboard focus. Mirrors the Figma `focused` variant.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables interaction and applies the disabled tokens.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.notes: Emitted when the user toggles the switch. Paired with `v-model`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import Switch from '@aziontech/webkit/switch'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const modelValue = ref(false)
</script>

<template>
  <Switch
    v-model="modelValue"
    aria-label="Toggle setting"
  />
</template>
